title: Safari Etiquette: How to Behave in the Parks
excerpt: How should you behave on safari? The basic rules for respecting wildlife, other visitors and the park.
body:
A safari is a privilege. These rules protect wildlife and make the experience better for everyone.

## In the vehicle

- Stay in the vehicle, except at designated places.
- Do not stand on the roof or sit on the window frame.
- Keep your voice low near animals.
- Do not ask the guide to drive off-road where this is not allowed.

## With animals

- Never feed animals.
- Keep distance, especially from animals with young.
- Do not block animals' paths.
- Avoid flash photography.

## With other visitors

- Give others a chance at a sighting; do not stay too long when vehicles are waiting.
- Do not play music.

## In the park

- Take all rubbish with you.
- Stick to the park's opening hours.
- Do not take souvenirs such as feathers, bones or plants.

## Your guide

Respect your guide's decisions. Good guides put animal welfare above the perfect photo.

Read [responsible travel tips](/blog/responsible-safari-tips/) or [plan your safari](/travel-proposal/).
